module_title: Greenhouse Effect, Global Warming, and Ozone Depletion
introduction: Our Earth is getting warmer, and our protective umbrella (the ozone layer) is thinning. This level explores the specific gases and chemicals responsible for these global crises.

core_concepts.title: The Greenhouse Effect
core_concepts.description: The natural process by which the Earth's atmosphere traps the sun's heat (Infrared radiation), keeping the planet warm enough to sustain life. Without it, Earth's average temperature would be $-18^\circ C$.

core_concepts.title: Major Greenhouse Gases (GHGs)
core_concepts.description:
1. Carbon Dioxide ($CO_2$): The most significant anthropogenic (human-made) gas (60% contribution). 
2. Methane ($CH_4$): 20% contribution. (Main sources: Paddy/rice fields, ruminant animals/cattle, marshes, and landfills). 
3. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs): 14% contribution. 
4. Nitrous Oxide ($N_2O$): 6% contribution (Laughing gas). 
*Note: Naturally, 'Water Vapor' is the largest contributor to the greenhouse effect.

core_concepts.title: Ozone Depletion
core_concepts.description:
The ozone layer ($O_3$) blocks harmful UV rays. 
Cause: CFCs (Chlorofluorocarbons), also known as 'Freons' (released from old refrigerators, ACs, and aerosol sprays). The 'Chlorine' (Cl) atom in CFCs acts as a catalyst, breaking down $O_3$ into $O_2$. 
Unit: The thickness of the ozone layer is measured in 'Dobson Units' (DU).

core_concepts.title: Important International Protocols
core_concepts.description:
1. Montreal Protocol (1987): An international treaty to protect the 'Ozone Layer' by banning the use of CFCs. 
2. Kyoto Protocol (1997): An international treaty aimed at reducing 'Greenhouse Gas' emissions to fight global warming.

important_entities.name: The Ozone Hole
important_entities.significance: In the 1980s, scientists discovered a massive thinning of the ozone layer (the 'Ozone Hole') specifically over 'Antarctica' (the South Pole). This happens due to the unique extreme cold and the formation of Polar Stratospheric Clouds (PSCs) during their winter.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Is Carbon Monoxide ($CO$) a greenhouse gas? Answer: NO! Carbon Dioxide ($CO_2$) is a greenhouse gas, but $CO$ is strictly a toxic primary pollutant; it does not significantly trap heat.

exam_strategy_tips: A famous UPSC/State PCS Prelims question: 'Which gas is primarily released from paddy (rice) fields?' Answer: Methane ($CH_4$).
